title: A vertical teaser by Friday
scenario:
A running-shoe brand wants a teaser for its social channels. The brief is in the exhibit. You plan to use a video model whose limits are also in the exhibit, copied from the vendor's docs on 2026-10-06.

It is Tuesday. The client reviews on Friday.
exhibit:
Client brief
  Shape: vertical 9:16
  Resolution: 1080p
  Length: 16 seconds, with sound
  Must show: the real shoe (3 product photos supplied)

Video model limits (vendor docs)
  Length: 4, 6 or 8 s; 1080p and 4k only at 8 s
  Shape: 16:9 or 9:16
  Reference images: up to 3; length must be 8 s
  Extension: +7 s per step, 720p only
  Videos per request: 1
  Wait: 11 s to 6 min
  Storage: 2 days on the server, then removed
  Status: Preview

questions.prompt: Which plan meets the brief within the model's limits?

options.text: One 16-second request at 1080p with the 3 product photos.
options.explanation: The longest single clip is 8 seconds. A 16-second request is outside the limits.

options.text: One 8-second 1080p clip, then extend it by 7 seconds twice.
options.explanation: Extension works only at 720p, so the result would not be 1080p.

options.text: Two 8-second 9:16 shots at 1080p, each using the product photos as references, cut together in an editor.
options.explanation: Right. 8 seconds is allowed at 1080p, reference images need 8-second clips, and two shots make 16 seconds.

options.text: Make a 16:9 video and crop it to vertical later.
options.explanation: The model can make 9:16 directly. Cropping a landscape clip throws away most of the frame and may cut the shoe.

questions.prompt: On Wednesday the clips are ready. A teammate says, "I'll download them on Monday after the review." What is the risk?

options.text: No risk. Generated videos stay in your account forever.
options.explanation: The exhibit says videos are kept for 2 days and then removed.

options.text: The videos are removed from the server after 2 days, so by Monday they may be gone.
options.explanation: Right. Google's Veo docs say to download your video within 2 days of generation.

options.text: The videos lose quality if they wait on the server.
options.explanation: The docs say nothing about quality loss. The risk is that the files are removed.

options.text: Nothing is lost: the 2-day limit applies only to videos you extend.
options.explanation: The docs say every generated video is removed after 2 days. Extending a video only resets that video's timer.

questions.prompt: The model's status is Preview. Your studio wants to use it for every client next year. What is the best way to plan?

options.text: Build everything around this one model. Popular models are never retired.
options.explanation: OpenAI's video API was shut down in 2026 with no one-to-one replacement. Popular models can be retired.

options.text: Avoid AI video until a model is guaranteed to last for years.
options.explanation: No vendor page offers that. Too strict: plan for change instead of waiting.

options.text: Use it, keep your shot descriptions and brand references in your own files, and check the vendor's deprecation page.
options.explanation: Right. Preview models can change, and deprecations are announced on vendor pages. Portable prompts let you move to another model.

options.text: Only use the Lite version, because Lite models last longer.
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs links Lite to a longer life. Lite also lacks 4k on this model.
